svg.title: Fabric Data Agent: Query-Generation Internals
svg.desc: An internals diagram. Four configuration surfaces — agent instructions, source instructions, source descriptions, and up to 100 example queries per source — feed an assembled prompt sent to a managed Azure OpenAI Assistant alongside the user's question and fetched schema. The assistant routes to one of four source-specific generators: NL2SQL for lakehouse/warehouse, NL2DAX for Power BI semantic models (no example-query support), NL2KQL for Eventhouse KQL databases, or Graph/GQL for ontology sources (three documented failure modes). A warning panel covers the Gold-in-Name-Only modeling antipattern that silently breaks NL2SQL. An accuracy-levers panel shows community benchmarking converging on instructions and data-model quality as the dominant factor, with measured accuracy reaching about 97.2% after fixing benchmark ground truth and tightening instructions. All four generator paths converge on a read-only, identity-scoped, governance-gated, 25-row-by-25-column-capped answer.
svg.text: What grounds the prompt, how the generator differs by source type, and what community benchmarking shows actually moves accuracy
CONFIGURATION SURFACES — what an agent author actually sets

g.title: Four configuration surfaces — agent instructions, source instructions, source descriptions, and example queries together shape agent behavior.
g.text: Agent-level instructions (≤15,000 chars): objective, source priority, terminology, response format
Data-source-level instructions: applies only after routing — relevant tables, columns, relationships
Data source description: the routing signal used to pick which of up to 5 sources answers a question
Templates: agent-level = Objective / Data sources / Terminology / Response guidelines / Common topics
source-level = General knowledge / Table descriptions / When asked about

g.title: Example queries (few-shot) — top-3 relevant examples looked up automatically per source; Power BI semantic models don't support this mechanism.
g.text: Top-3 auto-selected per question — except Power BI models

g.title: Assembled prompt — question, fetched schema, and creator instructions/examples merge here before the assistant selects a generator.
g.text: Assembled prompt → managed Azure OpenAI Assistant
User's question + schema fetched under the caller's own identity + instructions/examples above
The assistant then selects which source-specific generation tool to invoke, based on the routed source's type

svg.text: SOURCE-SPECIFIC GENERATORS — one prompt, four different code paths

g.title: NL2SQL (lakehouse / warehouse) — generates a read-only SQL statement against the SQL surface of the routed source.

g.aria-label: NL2DAX for Power BI semantic models
g.title: NL2DAX (semantic model) — generates DAX against a Power BI semantic model; Read permission suffices, RLS/CLS still applies; no example-query support.
g.text: Read permission is enough to run —

g.title: NL2KQL (Eventhouse) — generates KQL queried in place with no data movement; can reuse existing KQL UDFs; time-filter guidance for speed.
g.text: Queried in place — no data movement
Can reuse existing KQL UDFs and

g.aria-label: Graph or GQL for ontology sources
g.title: Graph / GQL (ontology) — generates a Microsoft Graph or GQL query; three field-reported failure modes distinct from SQL-based generators.
g.text: • needs binding names, not display names
• omits required dbo. prefix on SQL objects

g.title: All four generators converge here: identity-scoped execution, four-layer governance precedence, and a 25-row-by-25-column response cap.
g.text: Read-only query + governed answer — all four paths converge here
Executes under the caller's own identity, subject to four-layer governance precedence (tenant → workspace → developer → prompt)
Response capped at 25 rows × 25 columns, including follow-up turns — full request lifecycle in the companion orchestration diagram

g.aria-label: Warning: Gold in Name Only antipattern
g.title: Warning — GINO (Gold in Name Only): a superficially relabeled bronze table silently breaks NL2SQL agents.
g.text: A "gold" table that is only superficially relabeled bronze —
multi-grain facts, unnecessary normalization, outer joins —
silently breaks NL2SQL. A human analyst works around it;
the agent does not raise an error, it just answers wrong.
Fix: simplify toward Kimball-style star schemas.

g.aria-label: What actually moves accuracy — instructions and data-model quality
g.title: Accuracy levers — community benchmarking converges on instructions and data-model quality as the dominant factor, not the underlying model.
g.text: Instructions & data-model quality — the dominant lever
A side-by-side demo: identical source and model, one agent with
empty instructions, one fully instructed. On complex SCD2/bridge-
table questions, only the instructed agent answered correctly.
A 72-question multilingual benchmark initially scored lower — a
row-level audit found many failures traced to the benchmark's own
faulty ground truth, not the agent. After fixing the ground truth
AND tightening agent instructions, measured accuracy rose to:

svg.text: This diagram is the internals companion to two Fabric Codex diagrams:

"Fabric Data Agent Architecture" (source attach + governance shape) and "Life of a Fabric Data Agent Request" (full orchestration + failure branches). This one opens up the query-generation step those two treat as a single box.
Fabric Codex — original diagram, August 2026. Grounded in fabric-data-agent capability claims.
